works.abstract: Objectives: Nanoplastics (NP) are a growing global health concern posing risks to both wildlife and human health. Polystyrene plastics, commonly used in food packaging, can break down into smaller micro- and nanoplastics. These NP can contaminate food and beverages during production, processing, and from leaching of packaging. Further, NP have emerged as an environmental pollutant leading to animal consumption within their natural environments, and bioaccumulation up the food chain. While human exposure to NP continues through food, products, water, and air, the toxicity and implications for health have yet to be fully understood.
works.title: Polystyrene Nanoplastic Administration Alters Metabolic and Lipid Profiles in Peripheral Insulin-Sensitive Tissues
